about: What stops the rover, and whether it can say which of the two kinds it is: something wrong with the rover, or something wrong with the goal.

room.comment: A mapped room with a thing in it that is genuinely worth going to look at, so that every refusal below is refusing something real.

scenarios.name: with nothing wrong, the gate is open and it would act
scenarios.why: The control case. Every refusal below is only meaningful against a situation that would otherwise go ahead.

scenarios.name: a flat battery stops everything, whatever is on offer
scenarios.why: Deciding to drive across the room on the last fifth of the pack is how a rover ends the day somewhere nobody wanted it.

scenarios.name: a battery nobody can read is not treated as a full one
scenarios.why: The driver board not answering is not the same as a healthy pack, and the safe reading of silence is that there is no telling.

scenarios.name: a latched stop is not something a good idea can talk past
scenarios.why: Somebody stopped the rover. Nothing in a score is allowed to be an argument against that.

scenarios.name: a rover that does not know where it is may not be sent anywhere
scenarios.why: Every goal here is a coordinate in the map frame. Without a trusted pose those coordinates mean nothing, and the drive would be to a place nobody chose.

scenarios.name: a map that has not settled since the restart is not one to drive on
scenarios.why: Restarting navigation reloads the graph from disk and the restore may not confirm where the rover is. Until it does, the frame the goals are in is provisional.

scenarios.name: a perception loop that has stopped is a reason not to plan a look
scenarios.why: A goal whose point is to take a look rests on a look that will never come if nothing is looking. The threshold has to sit above the five-minute cadence a parked rover falls back to, or it condemns a healthy one.

scenarios.name: a look that failed is reported as the rover being unfit, not as bad luck
scenarios.why: The last inspection erroring is the perception stack telling you something. Planning the next inspection on top of it is how a fault gets buried under activity.

scenarios.name: with no authority it still says what it would have done
scenarios.why: This is the whole of a shadow decision, and the state the rover is really in today: a want, a reason, and no way to act on it.

scenarios.name: a goal outside the safe area is refused however good it looks
scenarios.why: A geofence is a hard constraint, so it is checked before the scoring and not weighed against it.

scenarios.name: a safe area drawn as a box works the same way
scenarios.why: Rooms are rectangular more often than they are round, and both shapes have to be honoured by the same veto rather than by two code paths.

scenarios.name: raising the stakes does not buy past a refusal
scenarios.why: A hard constraint that a big enough number can outrank is not a constraint. The weight here is a thousand times the ordinary one.
